bull_bear.body:
- India's largest C&I renewable energy provider; early mover shaping industry operating models
- 8%/12% share of annual C&I open-access RE additions in FY25/FY24
- 555 customers with 71.72% of contracted capacity from repeat customers; 94.72% customers rated A- or above
- PPAs with weighted-average tenure of 22.85 years and average lock-in of 16.86 years
- In-house execution across development, land, EPC, financing and asset management; premium pricing vs utility-scale peers
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- History of losses — Restated losses of ₹376.43m (FY24) and ₹594.73m (FY23) before turning profitable in FY25; some subsidiaries still loss-making
- Capital intensity and refinancing dependence — Large upfront project investment; ~2-year ramp to steady state; reliance on refinancing SPV debt on favourable terms
- Customer/counterparty concentration — Reliance on large technology customers and repeat customers for contracted capacity
- Execution/commissioning delays — Delays in achieving steady state or CoD could impair liquidity and debt repayment
- Regulatory/open-access policy dependence — Business economics hinge on state open-access, group-captive and transmission policies
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: CleanMax is a business-to-business renewable energy provider serving only commercial and industrial (C&I) customers, with 2.80 GW of operational, owned and managed capacity and 3.17 GW contracted-yet-to-be-executed as of October 31, 2025. It supplies renewable power under long-term PPAs/EAPAs and offers EPC, O&M and carbon-credit services across solar, wind and hybrid plants (Onsite within customer premises and Offsite in CleanMax-developed farms). Inception 2010; ~15 years of operating history.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Renewable Energy Power Sales:** Onsite Solar, Offsite STU-Connected (Group Captive / Third-Party Open Access), CTU/ISTS-Connected Offsite (EAPA)
- **Renewable Energy Services:** Capex Services (turnkey EPC + O&M), Carbon Services (I-RECs, carbon credits, advisory)

outlook.body: Constructing first CTU/ISTS-connected plants in Karnataka and Rajasthan to supply power pan-India; 3.17 GW of contracted-yet-to-be-executed capacity to be built out, plus scaling of the energy-attribute (EAPA/I-REC) business toward the 10-15 GW India market expected by 2030.

outlook.body:
- Segment mix shift toward Renewable Energy Power Sales (74% of FY25 revenue vs 51% in FY23)
- Heavy depreciation (non-cash) and high early-stage financing costs during 2-year project ramp
- SPV-level debt refinanced on better terms after steady-state; capital-intensive project development

risks.note: Flagged as a risk in the MD&A; the company also operates cross-border (Dubai, Bahrain, Thailand, Saudi Arabia) with at least one overseas subsidiary reporting in AED, creating currency translation/transaction exposure.
MD&A explicitly names supplier-related challenges and project execution risks as ongoing exposures for a business that must commission gigawatt-scale capacity annually.
Company flags changes in the regulatory environment as a risk factor, relevant given renewable power's dependence on state/central RE policy, grid connectivity and tariff regulation.
Company identifies land-acquisition as a risk to its construction pipeline, stating it has secured over 90% of the FY27 pipeline in advance specifically to neutralise this risk.
